title: Causal Modeling of Selection in Evolution

claims.paper_claim: Definition 1: the evolutionary selection model has four edge types.
claims.limitation: One hand-built T=2 graph checks edge presence; it does not validate the general definition, distributional semantics, or assumptions.

evidence.paper_claim: Definition 1: the evolutionary selection model has four edge types.
evidence.limitation: One hand-built T=2 graph checks edge presence; it does not validate the general definition, distributional semantics, or assumptions.

claims.paper_claim: Lemma 1: evolutionary selection can induce dependencies absent from the static graph.
claims.limitation: A larger G+ on two toy graphs is structural evidence only; it does not generate evolutionary data or establish the lemma for all DAGs.

evidence.paper_claim: Lemma 1: evolutionary selection can induce dependencies not present in the static graph.
evidence.limitation: A larger G+ on two toy graphs is structural evidence only; it does not generate evolutionary data or establish the lemma for all DAGs and distributions.

claims.paper_claim: Theorem 1: G+ represents the selected evolutionary d-separations.
claims.limitation: Only singleton A/B/C cases and empty conditioning sets on three hand-built graphs at T=2 are checked.

evidence.paper_claim: Theorem 1: the clique-augmented DAG represents the selected evolutionary d-separations.
evidence.limitation: Only singleton A/B/C cases and empty conditioning sets on three hand-built graphs at T=2 are checked; this is not a proof for arbitrary sets, generations, or model assumptions.

claims.paper_claim: Theorem 2: PC/GES interpretations are sound under the paper assumptions.
claims.limitation: The local oracle runs on G+ directly; it does not use observational data, PC/GES implementations, faithfulness checks, or precision experiments.

evidence.paper_claim: Theorem 2: PC/GES interpretations are sound under the paper's sampling and faithfulness assumptions.
evidence.limitation: This uses the repository's own d-separation oracle on G+, not observational data, the paper's PC/GES implementations, faithfulness checks, or precision experiments.

claims.paper_claim: Theorem 4: multi-domain identification is sound and complete.
claims.limitation: Both environments reuse the same graph and no data, domain shift, or CDNOD procedure is run.

evidence.paper_claim: Theorem 4: the multi-domain identification procedure has soundness and completeness guarantees.
evidence.limitation: Both environments reuse the same graph object and no data, domain shift, or CDNOD procedure is run; this is an internal consistency check, not multi-environment evidence.

claims.paper_claim: Section 5.2: seven real-world datasets support the method's interpretation.
claims.limitation: The seven datasets, preprocessing, learned graphs, and reported quantitative comparisons are absent from this checkout.

evidence.paper_claim: Section 5.2: results on seven real-world datasets support the method's interpretation.
evidence.limitation: The seven datasets, preprocessing, learned graphs, and reported quantitative comparisons are absent from this checkout.

gate_meaning: Ready for the documented finite-proxy scope; this gate is not evidence that the six paper claims or paper experiments were reproduced.
